The complete short original distinguishes changes due to treatment response from natural history and measurement effects. The methodological discussion contains no dried date fruit or separate dietary pain contrast.

The observational study uses a wearable and smartphone tool during exercises to assess pain and stiffness. It does not assign dried date fruit or separate an effect of consuming dates.

The clinical study evaluates pain and its relationship with freezing of gait and falls in Parkinson disease. The clinical outcomes are relevant in isolation. Dried dates were absent from the analyzed exposures.

The systematic review compares water-based passive therapy for different clinical outcomes, including pain. Dried date fruit was outside the evaluated interventions.

Processed tomato products combine forms and do not define a cooking intervention.
